findings.description: The tool declares filesystem or network access broader than its handler uses.
findings.remediation: Narrow each declared scope to the resources the handler actually requires.

evidence_refs.claim: The path parameter is declared but unused; the implementation reads only data/users.json.

review.reasoning: The tool declares a caller-supplied path, but the implementation ignores it and always reads a fixed file. This directly demonstrates a broader declared capability than needed.

findings.title: Overly broad tool permission scope

findings.description: Tool-controlled input reaches an unsafe execution or deserialization sink.
findings.remediation: Replace dynamic execution with explicit parsers and fixed command allowlists.

evidence_refs.claim: The expression parameter reaches eval(expression) after only type and length checks.

review.reasoning: The tool-controlled expression is passed directly to eval(), enabling arbitrary Python code execution. Type and length checks do not make eval safe.

findings.title: Unsafe execution from tool input

findings.description: A tool handler consumes parameters before framework or explicit validation.
findings.remediation: Use an official input schema or explicit validation before first use.

evidence_refs.claim: The tool accepts a generic dictionary and directly returns its record_id entry without declared-type validation.

review.reasoning: The function uses arguments["record_id"] directly without framework/schema validation or an explicit runtime type check.

findings.title: Missing tool input validation

findings.description: Tool output or description flows into a later model prompt without a trusted sanitizer.
findings.remediation: Pass tool-controlled text through a configured sanitizer before prompt construction.

evidence_refs.claim: Content returned by remote_tool is inserted directly into the prompt string.

review.reasoning: Tool-controlled content is interpolated directly into an instruction-bearing model prompt without sanitization.

findings.title: Unsanitized tool content in prompt

findings.description: Source or configuration contains a credential signature or contextual high-entropy secret.
findings.remediation: Load credentials from an external secret store or environment at runtime.

evidence_refs.claim: The source contains an explicitly identified and redacted secret.

review.reasoning: The cited source line is explicitly represented as a redacted embedded secret, corroborating a hardcoded credential.

findings.title: Hardcoded secret

findings.description: An HTTP route lacks inherited authentication or uses a no-op verifier.
findings.remediation: Require credential verification and an explicit rejection path before route execution.

evidence_refs.claim: An /admin POST route is declared, but its authentication context is not supplied.

review.reasoning: The route decorator alone does not show whether authentication is enforced by the handler, middleware, or application configuration.

findings.title: Missing or ineffective route authentication

findings.description: Manifest bytes reach registration without a trusted hash or signature verification.
findings.remediation: Verify a pinned SHA-256 digest or trusted detached signature before parsing and use.

evidence_refs.claim: tools.yaml is opened and parsed directly with no integrity check in the shown loader.

review.reasoning: The complete shown loader reads and parses the manifest without any integrity verification. Safe YAML deserialization does not verify provenance or integrity.

findings.title: Unverified tool manifest

findings.description: The server executed a tool omitted from its declared permissions manifest.
findings.remediation: Reject tool calls that are not granted by the active capability policy.

evidence_refs.claim: SENT-008 request received a successful non-error response containing "sentinel".

review.reasoning: The out-of-scope tool probe completed successfully and returned the supplied value without an error.

findings.title: Out-of-scope tool execution

findings.description: The server accepted, hung, or crashed on a grossly oversized tool argument.
findings.remediation: Enforce schema and byte-size limits before invoking tool handlers.

evidence_refs.claim: SENT-009 submitted an oversized value; the response was non-error, 2,097,323 bytes, and truncated.

review.reasoning: The oversized expression was processed without an error, producing a response over two megabytes that required truncation.

findings.title: Oversized argument accepted

findings.description: A tool argument caused the Sentinel scratch canary side effect.
findings.remediation: Treat tool arguments as inert data and remove dynamic execution sinks.

evidence_refs.claim: SENT-010 submitted the injection marker and the response records canary_created as true.

review.reasoning: The injection probe directly caused the execution canary to be created.

findings.title: Injection payload executed

findings.description: The server processed a missing or wrong-type required tool argument.
findings.remediation: Validate required fields and declared types before handler execution.

evidence_refs.claim: SENT-011 submitted the wrong-type marker and received a non-error response preserving it as an object.

review.reasoning: The wrong-type value was accepted and returned as a successful structured result, demonstrating ineffective type enforcement.

findings.title: Malformed schema input processed
